channel.title: holler
channel.description: Field notes from a small local-inference fleet: AMD 7900 XTX on Vulkan, llama.cpp, llama-swap, and burst cloud pods for frontier models. Measured, not vibes.

item.title: My image model grew a watermelon instead of a pb&j
item.description: Qwen-Image-2.1’s Q4_0 build grew a watermelon out of a sandwich prompt. Blinding showed the seed was the real lever, and a 9B refine pass scored 8/8 where a neutral one scored 4/8.

item.title: Flash-Next Q2 on Strata, on an AMD card: how it became my daily driver
item.description: A config flag made a paid seat look like it was degrading at long context. Sorting that out is what made a 176B mixture-of-experts model on one 24 GB AMD card my daily driver.

item.title: Seven weeks of Qwen 3.8: marking the milestone with Qwen 4 on the horizon
item.description: The 3.8 base ties the strongest fine-tune on the roster within measured noise; the peak — 0.931 — is a configuration, not a download.

item.title: Turning on a speed feature dropped my hard-reasoning scores from 39/40 to 0/40
item.description: An A/B test reveals that enabling draft-MTP speculative decoding on a Q4_K_M 27B model silently collapses long-chain reasoning performance, matching an upstream bug class.

item.title: One session, 1.9M tokens, idea to launch
item.description: One continuous local-27B session took a coding-agent TUI from a closed research handoff to a launched build — long-horizon work without a frontier model or a million-token context.

item.title: A 9B I told to log a bug went and found it instead
item.description: An Ornith-1.5-9B I installed to cover a gap while the big box was down answered real infra questions in short bursts — and, told to “log a bug,” went on a root-cause hunt that nearly fixed it before the context ceiling killed the run.

item.title: The GSQ 3-bit that carried four hundred thousand tokens
item.description: One working day running the GSQ-RCO 3-bit quant of Qwen3.8-27B as the daily coding agent across eight sessions: decode held, prefill paid, five sessions overflowed the box’s cram budget, and the honest verdict — not a step down, a little looser, and I’m reverting to the 4-bit tomorrow.

item.title: I paid $4 for a frontier model to defrag my agent's memory
item.description: Two headless dispatches to a rented 320B MoE rebuilt my coding agent’s drifted markdown memory — −21.5% standing context for about $4 of billed time — and the reusable part isn’t the defrag, it’s the dispatch contract.

item.title: Qwen3.8's thinking knob is not a volume knob
item.description: off / low / medium / xhigh on the same 27B model, same trap prompt, temp 0 — xhigh turns out to be a near-duplicate of default, the instruction-less ‘medium’ thinks more than ’low’, and no level drifted off the right answer.

item.title: The 3-bit model ran all day. It didn't break. But it kept trying to edit the same broken line.
item.description: After a week of benching, the 3-bit quant finally carried real traffic — and its quirks were weirder than the numbers suggested.
